To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a heterogeneous Co(CO) 4⊂Cr–MIL-101 catalyst for the ringexpansion carbonylation reaction of epoxides and demonstrated that this catalyst can be used for the continuous-flow synthesis of β-lactone products in a gas phase.
a Co(CO)-incorporated Cr(III)-MOF, Co(CO)-@Cr-MIL-100, can be used as a heterogeneous catalyst for the carbonylation of cyclic epoxides to β-lactone products.

the incorporation of the Co(CO) 4– ion into the pores of the Cr-MIL- 101 metal-organic framework leads to a heterogeneous catalyst for the gas-phase carbonylation of aliphatic and aromatic epoxides to β-lactone products, with a performance comparable to that of the reported homogeneous systems, thus providing the first example of a heterogeneous epoxide carbolyation catalyst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and application of heterogeneous catalysts based on metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for organic transformations.
the design and application of a new heterogeneous catalyst for the carbonylation of alcohols and epoxides.
the development of a heterogeneous catalyst system for the ring-expanding carbonylation of terminal epoxides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Co(CO)₄⁻-incorporated MOF catalyst exhibits the same catalytic performance as the homogeneous catalyst.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of heterogeneous epoxide carboloylation, and the potential of this approach to be scaled to continuous-flow operation.
the Co(CO)3+⊂Cr-MOF system represents a new paradigm for the development of heterogeneous catalysts that are active, selective, and stable in a broad range of catalytic reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heterogeneous Co(CO)3⊂Cr-MOF catalyst is a promising alternative to the homogeneous Co(CO)2PPh3 catalyst for the epoxide carbonylations.
we have developed an efficient heterogeneous catalyst for the production of β-lac-tones from epoxides by carbonylation, and the catalyst is based on an MOF.

we have developed a heterogeneous catalyst for epoxide carbonylations, which is the first such catalyst reported to date, and that this catalyst is capable of performing the reaction in a continuous fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cooperative ion-pair catalysis can be harnessed in a MOF to achieve a homogeneous-like reactivity in a heterogeneous system.

the combination of site-isolated Lewis acidity and cooperative ion-pair catalysis can be a viable strategy to develop heterogeneous catalysts with high activity and selectivity for reactions that require the presence of both Lewis and Brønsted acidic sites.
the incorporation of a homogeneous catalyst into a MOF can lead to a cooperative ion-pair catalysis, which can be harnessed for heterogeneous catalytic transformations.
